newsitem.title: USA: White House aide optimistic on US budget agreement.
newsitem.headline: White House aide optimistic on US budget agreement.

text.p: A White House aide Tuesday expressed optimism that a budget agreement would be reached this year with the Republican-dominated Congress.
"There is a feeling that we will get a budget agreement this year," John Hilley, assistant to the President and White House director of legislative affairs, said.
He said that currently the White House is unwilling to move off its proposal for a capital gains tax cut for home owners. Republicans in Congress are seeking a more broad-based capital gains tax cut.
"We have a capital gains tax cut proposal on the table which goes to the ownership. At this time, we are unwilling to move off that," Hilley told reporters after speaking to a tax conference.
He said the five working groups that were formed to work on key issues, such as taxes, education and the District of Columbia, would likely start meeting next week.

"We hope to start all the working groups as early as next week," he said. The working groups were formed after President Clinton met with Congressional leaders to discuss priorities for this year, and the groups will include members of Congress and administration officials.
